original_plan.expected_observation: The native episode closes without selection because no owned replay has a passing complete acceptance evaluation and the backend-solve budget has zero remaining units.
original_plan.fixed_conditions: All original ten load cases, shared physical structure, gravity, timing, solver settings, qualification thresholds, evaluator bounds, initialization protocol, and failure-retention policy remained frozen.
original_plan.hypothesis: Within the finite tested set of legal straight frictionless base-anchored tendon architectures, redundant full-length restraint does not yield the required local-compliance/global-restraint separation; mixed endpoint spans improve settling and isolation but still miss displacement and static-balance requirements. This closes the tested route under the frozen budget, not the broader design family.
original_plan.interpretation: The two mathematical mechanism requests were executed and retained but ended in TypeError, so they provide no verified physical quantity. Physical alternatives executed were the default stiff baseline; an 8-tendon full-span compliant design; 12 redundant full-span tendons; mixed mid/full spans; a four-endpoint lattice; counter-helical full spans; and a programmed-payout S-curve initialization attempt. Mixed mid/full endpoints had the best information value and improved loaded speed and the tip/local ratio, while redundant full-span and endpoint-lattice escalation added little and the counter-helical route destabilized response. The final S-curve branch failed before equilibrium and supplies no trajectory evidence. Further legal geometry, stiffness, and payout combinations remain plausible, but no backend solves remain to test them under the frozen protocol. Closure is budget-forced and finite, not an impossibility claim.
original_plan.stopping_condition: Stop because 80 of 80 backend solves are consumed, zero remain, and none of the complete ten-case physical evaluations passed acceptance.
original_plan.weakening_observation: A newly authorized physical budget, a complete passing replay, or a new legal mechanism that simultaneously raises local displacement above 0.01 m and lowers tip and static-balance errors would weaken this finite-route closure.
